notes: Four own pages read, all HTTP 200 and not thin (home, pricing-plans, integrations, about-us). The pricing page shows Standard, Pro and Ultimate with Request pricing and no dollar amounts, so every dollar figure ($65, $65 per user, $225) and the per-user basis are unverifiable. C07 and C08 (a free Lite plan for up to 2 users) are left unverifiable: the pricing page lists no free or Lite plan and offers a 7-day free trial, but it does not explicitly rule out a free plan; a reviewer may prefer wrong if the complete plan list is taken as explicit. Google Local Services Ads and RingCentral (C16, C17) are absent from the integrations page, which loads its full list in the text; absence was not treated as contradiction. The pricing FAQ says a built-in phone system comes with all plans while the plan table marks Genius Phone as sold separately; C09 follows the add-on wording the answers use. Capability descriptions (call tracking, AI scheduling, offline mode) were not coded. No claim is wrong or stale, so no cited page was read for causes. Pass 2 (8 Oct 2026): no browser reads exist for this vendor. Completeness: two instances added (q4 Claude run 1 to C07 and C08) and eight claims added (C23 to C30) from table cells and pricing lines under the vendor's sub-headings. Two of the new claims are wrong: C27 (a 14-day free trial; the pricing page FAQ says 7 days; cause not found) and C28 (online booking costs extra; the plan comparison includes it in every plan; cause: the cited FieldPulse Workiz-alternatives article, which carries the same sentence). That sentence was split because call tracking (C29, the page both includes the phone system in all plans and marks Genius Phone sold separately) and automation (C30) are not settled. Six cited pages were read for causes: fieldpulse.com, thedigitalprojectmanager.com (HTTP 403, listed in needs_browser_read), getonecrew.com, serviceagent.ai, the vendor's own Jobber-alternatives blog and fieldservicesoftware.io. For the reviewer: the vendor's own blog lists Workiz pricing starting at about $187 per month (annual, 3 users included) and a 7-day trial; that figure is approximate and annual, so it was not used to re-class the $65 and $225 starting prices (C02, C04) or the $187 Kickstart price (C23), which stay unverifiable against the pricing page's Request pricing. C29 sits in tension with C09 (classed true in pass 1 from the sold separately wording).
